title: Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan to inaugurate the fifth edition of Kashi Tamil Sangamam 5.0
subtitle: KTS 5.0 to be held from November 28 to December 12, 2026 in Varanasi
body_text: Vice-President of India, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan, will inaugurate the fifth edition of Kashi Tamil Sangamam (KTS) to be held from 28 November to 12 December 2026, in Varanasi. Union Minister for Defence, Shri Rajnath Singh, is scheduled to attend the valedictory session. The Event will bring together over 1,400 delegates to celebrate the centuries-old cultural, linguistic and civilisational ties between Tamil Nadu and Kashi. The initiative, inspired by the vision of Prime Minister, Shri Narendra Modi, seeks to strengthen the bonds between the two regions and promote the spirit of Ek Bharat Shreshtha Bharat . The fifth edition will celebrate the timeless wisdom and ethical teachings of the Thirukkural , one of the most celebrated works of Tamil literature. The Event is organized by the Department of Higher Education, Union Ministry of Education, in collaboration with IIT Madras, Banaras Hindu University (BHU), Central Institute of Classical Tamil (CICT), Uttar Pradesh Government and several Central Govt Departments and Ministries. Theme for KTS 5.0 - “Thirukkural Payilvom – Thirukkural Abhyas Karen” The theme of Kashi Tamil Sangamam 5.0 is “Thirukkural Payilvom – Thirukkural Abhyas Karen”, meaning “Let us Learn the Thirukkural”. The focus is on fostering awareness and understanding of the timeless wisdom of the Thirukkural , particularly among students and youth, while encouraging appreciation of India's rich literary traditions and enduring cultural heritage. The Thirukkural , authored by the celebrated Tamil poet and philosopher Thiruvalluvar, is one of the most enduring works of Tamil literature and continues to offer guidance across generations. Its 1,330 couplets explore ethics, governance, human relationships, compassion, discipline and responsible living. The text is divided into three parts, Aram (Virtue), Porul (Wealth) and Inbam (Love), encompassing the principles of righteous conduct, social and political life, and human relationships. Delegates and Itinerary Around 1,400 participants from Tamil Nadu, organised into seven groups of around 200 persons each, will undertake an eight-day journey. It comprises four days of travel and four days of visits and structured programmes. The itinerary covers Varanasi, Prayagraj and Ayodhya, with cultural, academic, domain-specific and spiritual engagements. The participants come from seven categories: • Students • Teachers • Writers and Media Professionals • Agriculture and Allied Sectors • Professionals and Artisans • Women • Spiritual leaders During their stay in Varanasi, delegates will visit prominent religious, historical and cultural sites, including Kashi Vishwanath Temple, Ramnagar Fort and Bharat Mata Temple. The itinerary also includes Ganga Aarti, Ganga Snan, academic sessions and cultural programmes. Delegates will subsequently visit the Triveni Sangam in Prayagraj and Shri Ram Temple in Ayodhya. A special Tamil heritage circuit will take delegates to Mahakavi Subramania Bharati’s ancestral house, Kedar Ghat and Kashi Matham in Little Tamil Nadu, along with an academic interaction at BHU’s Tamil Department. Students' Engagement Programme A nationwide Students' Engagement Programme is being undertaken through 1,000 Higher Education Institutions to promote wider understanding of the Thirukkural among students from diverse academic disciplines and linguistic backgrounds. It will include structured study, research, and campus-based activities. •Each participating institution will assess its interested students on the Thirukkural and nominate one student on merit. •The selected students will attend an online academic orientation, offered in 22 scheduled languages and English. •A one-month research and academic engagement will follow, with multilingual study material from CICT. Each eligible selected student will be entitled to a stipend of ₹10,000, subject to the programme guidelines and completion of the prescribed requirements. •Each student will write an article or research note of 4 to 10 pages under a faculty guide and give a one-hour presentation on the Thirukkural at their institution. Thirukkural Teaching in Schools of Uttar Pradesh During the Sangamam, 50 teachers from Tamil Nadu will visit Uttar Pradesh and teach the Thirukkural in schools. Thirukkural experts from Tamil Nadu will also visit schools in Varanasi. They will introduce students to the core values of the text through orientation modules, interactive sessions and quizzes. Reading Sessions in Schools The National Book Trust, in association with the Rashtriya e-Pustakalaya, will conduct interactive sessions in schools in Varanasi on reading habits, storytelling and creative activities. Academic Engagements, Cultural Showcases and Regional Craft Exhibitions Banaras Hindu University will co-host a National Conference on the Thirukkural , with the Bharatiya Bhasha Samiti as a partner. Cultural programmes and screenings of short films on the Thirukkural will also be organized. Handicraft and handloom outlets from Tamil Nadu and Uttar Pradesh will be set up for the delegates at the main venue. Digital and Public Outreach Kashi Tamil Sangamam 5.0 will also use technology to make the teachings of the Thirukkural accessible to a wider audience across India. The Thirukkural multilingual app of CICT carries all 1,330 couplets with translations into 22 scheduled languages. CICT's programme for the Edition also includes short animated videos and films on selected couplets, and Thirukkural audiobooks.
